"The Middle" is a song by Russian-German record producer Zedd, American country music singer Maren Morris, and American musical duo Grey. It was written by Sarah Aarons, The Monsters and the Strangerz, Grey and Zedd with production handled by the latter three. The song was released commercially for digital download and streaming on 23 January 2018 by Interscope Records. It reached number one in Singapore and the top ten in the US, the UK and several other countries. It was nominated for Record of the Year, Song of the Year, and Best Pop Duo/Group Performance at the 61st Annual Grammy Awards.

sections.heading: Release
sections.wikitext:
The song was first revealed in an accompanying interview of Zedd's cover shot for ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'', published on 10 August 2017. Zedd played interviewer Chris Martins unreleased material in a studio, one of which was "The Middle", which featured co-writer [[Sarah Aarons]] as a demo singer.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Martins|first=Chris|title=Zedd, Dance Music's Anti-Bro, on Making Hits for Selena, Kesha and Liam and Why DJs Should 'Speak Up' On Trump|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/cover-story/7896990/zedd-interview-billboard-cover-story-2017|access-date=23 January 2018|magazine=Billboard|date=10 August 2017}}</ref>

On 11 January 2018, Zedd teased the song on [[social media]], saying: "Hey guys, it's that time again. I wanted to show you a preview to my brand new song. Check it out," after which he played a short snippet of the song.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Bein|first=Kat|title=Zedd (Sort Of) Teased His New Single: Watch|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/dance/8094108/zedd-new-single-teaser-clip|magazine=Billboard|date=12 January 2018|access-date=23 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Meadow|first=Matthew|title=Zedd Posts Maddeningly Short Clip Of His Next Single To Tease Fans|url=http://www.youredm.com/2018/01/11/zedd-posts-maddeningly-short-clip-next-single-tease-fans/|work=Your EDM|date=11 January 2018|access-date=22 January 2018}}</ref> The collaboration was officially announced via social media on 19 January 2018, along with the single artwork,<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Bein|first=Kat|title=Zedd Announces 'The Middle' With Maren Morris & Grey|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/dance/8095144/zedd-the-middle-maren-morris-grey|magazine=Billboard|date=19 January 2018|access-date=23 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Sterling|first=Scott|title=Zedd & Maren Morris Announce New Collaboration 'The Middle'|url=http://news.radio.com/2018/01/19/zedd-maren-morris-the-middle/|work=[[CBS Radio]]|date=19 January 2018|access-date=23 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180330154823/http://news.radio.com/2018/01/19/zedd-maren-morris-the-middle/|archive-date=30 March 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> which Zedd teased a day earlier without a title on it.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Bein|first=Kat|title=Zedd Teases Artwork on Twitter, Fueling New Music Speculation|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/dance/8094959/zedd-artwork-new-music-2018|magazine=Billboard|date=18 January 2018|access-date=23 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Macke|first=Johnni|title=Zedd May Have Just Dropped A Big New Music Hint|url=http://peopleschoice.com/2018/01/18/zedd-teases-possible-new-music/|work=[[People's Choice Awards]]|date=18 January 2018|access-date=23 January 2018}}</ref>
sections.text:
The song was first revealed in an accompanying interview of Zedd's cover shot for Billboard, published on 10 August 2017. Zedd played interviewer Chris Martins unreleased material in a studio, one of which was "The Middle", which featured co-writer Sarah Aarons as a demo singer.

On 11 January 2018, Zedd teased the song on social media, saying: "Hey guys, it's that time again. I wanted to show you a preview to my brand new song. Check it out," after which he played a short snippet of the song. The collaboration was officially announced via social media on 19 January 2018, along with the single artwork, which Zedd teased a day earlier without a title on it.

sections.heading: Collaboration
sections.wikitext:
Zedd explained in a press release that they "worked really hard on this record to get it just right". He also opened up about the opportunity to work with both collaborators, saying that working with [[Maren Morris]] was "super fun because she is clearly an amazing singer and very talented musician", and that he loves working with Grey because they strive to "make the best music possible".

Morris added: "Zedd was so great to work with and so easy-going, it felt like we'd been working together for years. The sound is reflective of my many influences as an artist – a little bit country, little pop, little R&B, relatable, emotional and catchy as hell. There are no limits with this song and I can't wait to see how the fans react." She revealed in a statement that she recorded her vocal for the song with Zedd in Nashville "several weeks ago" before the song's release. Grey admitted that they faced a few obstacles during production, but they "kept fighting for it" because the song was special.<ref>{{cite news|last=Sands|first=Nicole|title=Zedd, Maren Morris and Grey Team Up with Target to Debut New Single 'The Middle'|url=http://people.com/music/zedd-maren-morris-grey-target-debut-the-middle-grammys-2018/|work=[[People (magazine)|People]]|date=23 January 2018|access-date=23 January 2018}}</ref>

sections.heading: Vocal demos
sections.wikitext:
[[Demi Lovato]], [[Camila Cabello]], [[Anne-Marie (singer)|Anne-Marie]], [[Carly Rae Jepsen]], [[Tove Lo]], [[Bishop Briggs]], [[Bebe Rexha]], [[Lauren Jauregui]], [[Daya (singer)|Daya]], [[Charli XCX]], [[Elle King]], [[Elley Duhé]] and [[Lennon Stella]] all recorded demos of the song before Morris' version was selected.

Stefan Johnson, one-fifth of production team The Monsters and the Strangerz, stated that "it was a super long process." Jordan Johnson of the same team added: "We never lost the feeling for that song. Even a year later, I, as a creator hadn't gotten tired of it. It was special."<ref name="Halperin">{{cite news|last=Halperin|first=Shirley|title='The Middle' Is a Hit for Marren Moris, After Demi, Camila, Bebe Don't Make the Cut|url=https://variety.com/2018/music/news/zedd-the-middle-singers-maren-morris-camila-cabello-demi-lovato-carly-rae-jepsen-1202778917/|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=23 April 2018|access-date=23 April 2018}}</ref>

The first iteration of the song (before Zedd and Grey were attached) was intended to be a single for Lovato (who had released a song with the same name on her 2008 album ''[[Don't Forget]]''), but she passed after deciding the song was "too pop" and opted to release "[[Sorry Not Sorry (Demi Lovato song)|Sorry Not Sorry]]" instead.<ref name="Halperin"/> Once Zedd and Grey were brought on board, Cabello's version was selected but she pulled out two weeks prior to the song's release in order to focus on promoting "[[Havana (Camila Cabello song)|Havana]]".<ref name="Halperin"/> After Cabello backed out, Anne-Marie's version was chosen but she had to back out due to conflicts stemming from the release of "[[Friends (Marshmello and Anne-Marie song)|Friends]]".<ref name="Halperin"/> After plans to release Anne-Marie's version fell through, the production team discovered that Morris had recorded a version but that it was never reviewed when initially submitted for consideration.<ref name="Halperin"/> Once the production team heard Morris' version, it was selected for the final cut.

Rexha's demo leaked online in 2018,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://genius.com/Bebe-rexha-the-middle-lyrics|title=The Middle - Bebe Rexha (Demo)|publisher=[[Genius (website)|Genius]]|accessdate=5 January 2023}}</ref> Cabello's demo leaked in 2020<ref>{{cite web|url=https://genius.com/Camila-cabello-the-middle-lyrics|title=The Middle - Camila Cabello (Demo)|publisher=[[Genius (website)|Genius]]|accessdate=5 January 2023}}</ref> while Lovato's,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://genius.com/Demi-lovato-the-middle-demo-lyrics|title=The Middle - Demi Lovato (Demo)|publisher=[[Genius (website)|Genius]]|accessdate=21 December 2021}}</ref> XCX's<ref>{{cite web|url=https://genius.com/Charli-xcx-the-middle-lyrics|title=The Middle - Charli XCX (Demo)|publisher=[[Genius (website)|Genius]]|accessdate=5 January 2023}}</ref> and Briggs' demos leaked in 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://genius.com/Bishop-briggs-the-middle-demo-lyrics|title=The Middle - Bishop Briggs (Demo)|publisher=[[Genius (website)|Genius]]|accessdate=5 January 2023}}</ref> Sarah Aarons' original demo leaked online in 2022,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://genius.com/Sarah-aarons-the-middle-lyrics|title=The Middle - Sarah Aarons (Demo)|publisher=[[Genius (website)|Genius]]|accessdate=5 January 2023}}</ref> including the demo of her second rendition have also leaked in 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://genius.com/Sarah-aarons-the-middle-demo-2-lyrics|title=The Middle - Sarah Aarons (Demo 2)|publisher=[[Genius (website)|Genius]]|accessdate=3 January 2024}}</ref> Anne-Marie's full demo leaked online in 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://genius.com/Anne-marie-the-middle-lyrics|title=The Middle - Anne-Marie (Demo)|publisher=[[Genius (website)|Genius]]|accessdate=3 January 2024}}</ref>
sections.text:
Demi Lovato, Camila Cabello, Anne-Marie, Carly Rae Jepsen, Tove Lo, Bishop Briggs, Bebe Rexha, Lauren Jauregui, Daya, Charli XCX, Elle King, Elley Duhé and Lennon Stella all recorded demos of the song before Morris' version was selected.

Stefan Johnson, one-fifth of production team The Monsters and the Strangerz, stated that "it was a super long process." Jordan Johnson of the same team added: "We never lost the feeling for that song. Even a year later, I, as a creator hadn't gotten tired of it. It was special."

The first iteration of the song (before Zedd and Grey were attached) was intended to be a single for Lovato (who had released a song with the same name on her 2008 album Don't Forget), but she passed after deciding the song was "too pop" and opted to release "Sorry Not Sorry" instead. Once Zedd and Grey were brought on board, Cabello's version was selected but she pulled out two weeks prior to the song's release in order to focus on promoting "Havana". After Cabello backed out, Anne-Marie's version was chosen but she had to back out due to conflicts stemming from the release of "Friends". After plans to release Anne-Marie's version fell through, the production team discovered that Morris had recorded a version but that it was never reviewed when initially submitted for consideration. Once the production team heard Morris' version, it was selected for the final cut.

Rexha's demo leaked online in 2018, Cabello's demo leaked in 2020 while Lovato's, XCX's and Briggs' demos leaked in 2021. Sarah Aarons' original demo leaked online in 2022, including the demo of her second rendition have also leaked in 2023. Anne-Marie's full demo leaked online in 2023.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: Kat Bein of ''Billboard'' opined that the song is "relatively sparse with cute, lively flourishes", writing that it has "definite sonic similarities" to Zedd's previous song "[[Stay (Zedd and Alessia Cara song)|Stay]]".<ref name="Billboard">{{cite magazine|last=Bein|first=Kat|title=Zedd, Maren Morris & Grey Lose Their Heads Over Love on 'The Middle': Listen|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/dance/8095509/zedd-new-song-maren-morris-grey-the-middle-lyric-video|magazine=Billboard|date=23 January 2018|access-date=24 January 2018}}</ref> ''[[Rolling Stone]]''{{'}}s Brittney McKenna deemed the song "an infectious earworm" in which Morris "strays from her country roots". She felt that the "Nineties R&B-indebted, vocoder-driven chorus" recalls the sound of "Stay", and that Morris "deftly occupies the new, poppy space".<ref>{{cite magazine|last=McKenna|first=Brittney|title=Hear Maren Morris Sing on Vibrant New Zedd Song 'The Middle'|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/country/news/hear-maren-morris-sing-on-vibrant-new-zedd-song-the-middle-w515781|magazine=Rolling Stone|date=23 January 2018|access-date=24 January 2018}}</ref> Hugh McIntyre of [[Fuse (TV channel)|Fuse]] found Morris' appearance on the track surprising, "considering the genres she primarily works in", as he praised Morris for "supplying vocals perfectly". He felt that it "leans a lot more pop than electro", which makes the song more appealing to a broader variety of listeners. Regarding the song "an easy-to-love electronic smash" and "a slightly reductive mix" of "Stay" and "[[Starving (song)|Starving]]", he noted that it is "not entirely original" due to its "reminiscence of what the musicians have delivered before".<ref>{{cite news|last=McIntyre|first=Hugh|title=Zedd Borrows From Past Hits for New Maren Morris-Assisted Single 'The Middle': Listen|url=https://www.fuse.tv/2018/01/zedd-maren-morris-grey-new-single|work=Fuse|date=23 January 2018|access-date=24 January 2018}}</ref> Similarly, Madeline Roth of [[MTV News]] called the song "a poppy earworm" and a combination of "Stay" and "Starving", which is "catchy as hell and practically destined for radio domination".<ref>{{cite news|last=Roth|first=Madeline|title=Maren Morris Goes Pop On Zedd's Addictive New Song 'The Middle'|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/3060203/maren-morris-zedd-grey-the-middle/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180125015442/http://www.mtv.com/news/3060203/maren-morris-zedd-grey-the-middle/|url-status=dead|archive-date=25 January 2018|work=MTV News|date=23 January 2018|access-date=24 January 2018}}</ref> Mike Nied of [[Idolator (website)|Idolator]] wrote that the song "blends elements of country and EDM" and praised Morris for providing "impassioned vocals".<ref>{{cite news|last=Nied|first=Mike|title=Zedd Teams Up With Maren Morris & Grey On Their Infectious "The Middle"|url=https://www.idolator.com/7674012/zedd-maren-morris-grey-the-middle|work=Idolator|date=23 January 2018|access-date=24 January 2018}}{{dead link|date=August 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Billy Dukes of Taste of Country described the song as "an unlikely combination of EDM, '90s pop and modern country music".<ref>{{cite news|last=Dukes|first=Billy|title=Maren Morris Makes EDM Debut With Zedd, 'The Middle' [Listen]|url=http://tasteofcountry.com/maren-morris-zedd-the-middle-edm-debut/|work=Taste of Country|date=23 January 2018|access-date=24 January 2018}}</ref>
sections.text: Kat Bein of Billboard opined that the song is "relatively sparse with cute, lively flourishes", writing that it has "definite sonic similarities" to Zedd's previous song "Stay". Rolling Stone{{'}}s Brittney McKenna deemed the song "an infectious earworm" in which Morris "strays from her country roots". She felt that the "Nineties R&B-indebted, vocoder-driven chorus" recalls the sound of "Stay", and that Morris "deftly occupies the new, poppy space". Hugh McIntyre of Fuse found Morris' appearance on the track surprising, "considering the genres she primarily works in", as he praised Morris for "supplying vocals perfectly". He felt that it "leans a lot more pop than electro", which makes the song more appealing to a broader variety of listeners. Regarding the song "an easy-to-love electronic smash" and "a slightly reductive mix" of "Stay" and "Starving", he noted that it is "not entirely original" due to its "reminiscence of what the musicians have delivered before". Similarly, Madeline Roth of MTV News called the song "a poppy earworm" and a combination of "Stay" and "Starving", which is "catchy as hell and practically destined for radio domination". Mike Nied of Idolator wrote that the song "blends elements of country and EDM" and praised Morris for providing "impassioned vocals". Billy Dukes of Taste of Country described the song as "an unlikely combination of EDM, '90s pop and modern country music".

sections.heading: Commercial performance
sections.wikitext: The song reached No. 5 on ''Billboard'' [[Hot 100]].<ref>{{cite magazine |url= https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/2018-04-28 |title=The Hot 100|date=28 April 2018 |magazine=Billboard }}</ref> As of February 2019, it had sold 771,000 copies in the United States.<ref name="sales">{{cite news|url=http://roughstock.com/news/2019/02/43659-top-30-digital-country-singles-sales-chart-february-20-2019|title=Top 30 Digital Country Singles Sales Chart: February 20, 2019|work=RoughStock|first=Matt |last=Bjorke |date= 20 February 2019 |access-date=24 March 2019 }}</ref> In January 2021, "The Middle" surpassed 1 billion streams on [[Spotify]],<ref>{{Cite tweet|number=1352360572596051970|user=Zedd|title=Today marks an unbelievable milestone for me. "The Middle" w/ @greymusic and @marenmorris just passed 1 BILLION streams on @spotify!!!|date=21 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=21 January 2021|title='The Middle' becomes Zedd's first song to surpass 1 billion Spotify streams|url=https://dancingastronaut.com/2021/01/the-middle-becomes-zedds-first-song-to-surpass-1-billion-spotify-streams/|access-date=23 January 2021|website=Dancing Astronaut|language=en-US}}</ref> the first song to do so for all three artists.<ref>{{Cite web|date=21 January 2021|title=Zedd Secures His First Billion-Play Song On Spotify With Grey, Maren Morris Collab, "The Middle"|url=https://www.youredm.com/2021/01/21/zedd-secures-his-first-billion-play-song-on-spotify-with-grey-maren-morris-collab-the-middle/|access-date=23 January 2021|website=Your EDM|language=en-US}}</ref>
sections.text: The song reached No. 5 on Billboard Hot 100. As of February 2019, it had sold 771,000 copies in the United States. In January 2021, "The Middle" surpassed 1 billion streams on Spotify, the first song to do so for all three artists.
